sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Production and Global Distribution of Vertical Micro-Dramas

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with elements of Commercial Law (Unitary National System)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–China Double Tax Avoidance Agreement (DTA) of 1982, as amended by the Protocol of 2014
Luxembourg–United States Double Tax Avoidance Agreement (DTA) of 1996, as amended by Protocol of 2004
Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) investment and trade agreements
European Union Membership (EU treaties and capital movement liberalisation)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Act of 12 November 2004 on the prevention and use of the financial system for money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Act of 25 March 2020; the Act of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); the Luxembourg Act of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (for SCSp formation and UBO obligations); CSSF Regulation 12-02 on AML/CFT procedures; circulars of the Luxembourg Bar and Institute of Chartered Accountants.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner exceeding the 25% threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner (utility bill or bank statement issued within last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated bank in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or notarized translation, depending on country of origin; consular legalization where the country is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / professional reference letter confirming source of funds and source of wealth of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution or licensed legal/accounting professional
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not in apostille bundle generally; verified directly by the Luxembourg notary or RBE filing agent; if signed abroad for corporate entities, Hague Apostille required for any corporate power of attorney so used

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the constitutional and beneficial ownership repartition document (e.g., partnership agreement draft) for the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary or foreign legal professional (for foreign entities acting as SCSp partner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and legalisation for all foreign public documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory preliminary screening of all UBOs and proposed managers against: (1) the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, (2) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions lists, (3) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, (4) the Luxembourg Office of Foreign Assets Control implementing lists (Ministère des Affaires étrangères et européennes), and (5) domestic PEP databases maintained by the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and the CSSF. Given the low-risk standard profile of a vertical micro-drama streaming app, standard customer due diligence is performed, but enhanced due diligence automatically applies if any party is a domestic/international PEP, or is linked to high-risk jurisdictions. All screening results are documented and retained for a minimum of five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBRC) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online filing portal: www.lbrc.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name of an SCSp may be expressed in French, German, Luxembourgish, or in a language commonly used in international commerce (including English), provided that the legal form designation is unequivocally rendered. The name must contain the abbreviation 'SCSp' or the full French form 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'. The name must be distinct from any other name appearing in the RCS database. If a name is expressed using non-Latin characters, a French transliteration must be submitted. Any correctly filed name is accepted without need for local-language translation, but French remains the official language of the registry for the articles of association and all mandatory filings.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking (requires prior CSSF authorisation)
État / State / Government (misleading implication of public authority)
Charitable words implying registered non-profit status (e.g., 'Fondation' without proper foundation registration)
Facility/Estate words suggesting real estate investment guarantee (e.g., 'Immobilier de Prestige' needing prior registration)
Flags or emblems of the Grand Duchy (use of Luxembourg national coats of arms or logos)
Fiduciaire / Trust Company / Trustee (requires licensing or special status under Luxembourg law)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS issues a provisional rejection, the applicant or its notary may submit a written rebuttal directly to the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés within 15 calendar days of the rejection notice. The appeal must explain why the proposed name does not violate the distinctiveness or prohibited-terms provisions, and may include legal argument and supporting documentation (e.g., trademark registration or prior use evidence). The RCS must issue a final decision within one month. An unsuccessful applicant may further appeal to the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months, following the procedure under Luxembourg law of 21 June 1999 on civil procedure. For practical expediency, a revised name application can be filed immediately after an initial rejection; the initial reservation window is automatically lifted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office solutions are not generally accepted for an SCSp. Luxembourg law requires that the SCSp maintain an effective registered office in Luxembourg, being a physical address identifiable in the RCS. A virtual office may serve ancillary or correspondence functions but cannot replace a real operational location for statutory purposes. The Luxembourg anti-abuse authorities and notaries will verify that the registered office corresponds to a genuine principal place of management or control of the SCSp, especially when the corporate purpose includes production and global distribution of digital content, which can have minimal physical footprint.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate (15% likelihood within first three years). Luxembourg authorities increasingly conduct selective verification of registered offices to deter letterbox arrangements; a SCSp whose sole business is international digital distribution may invite additional substance review under the Luxembourg Circular L.G.-A no. 42 (AT ADR) and anti-abuse doctrine. However, the absence of a mandatory license for the production and distribution of vertical micro-dramas and the low AML risk tier keep the expected inspection probability at a manageable 15%. The risk can be further mitigated by appointing in-country management, retaining board minutes, and maintaining a physical document/records presence in Luxembourg.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg RCS company name reservation and publication fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via LBRC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCS tariff schedule for name reservation and preliminary filing (approximately EUR 300–350)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Civil-law notary fees for drafting and authenticating the notarial deed of the SCSp establishment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Luxembourg notarial tariff (tarif des notaires) based on partnership capital; base fee for standard private SCSp documents ranges EUR 1,000–1,500, excluding VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register filing and ongoing UBO data file maintenance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBRC) and RCS deputy
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RBE filing fee (EUR 278 as per the 13 January 2019 Law; indexed in 2025)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO PEP and OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening package (per UBO, standard due diligence)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party AML/know-your-customer provider engaged by the certification agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fee per UBO (USD 150–300 per individual under standardized screening)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and translation services for foreign-issued UBO documents (2 passports and 2 address proofs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign apostille authorities and certified translation agency in Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Apostille per document (typically USD 20–60) plus Luxembourg translation fee (USD 45–55 per standard page)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office arrangement and sealed corporate mailbox in Luxembourg City (annual, first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered office services provider in Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a physical registered office in Luxembourg (approx. USD 780–1,200/year); virtual-only provider will not suffice for SCSp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel fee for pre-incorporation due diligence, SCSp partnership agreement drafting, and AML/CFT policy design
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / certified ELP attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg market hourly rates for corporate boutique firms (USD 350–450/hour; estimated 12–15 hours for low-risk micro-drama vehicle)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statistical and indirect administrative charges (tax registration file, VAT simulation, social security registration of managers if needed)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Direct Tax Authorities (ACD) and Registre National des Personnes Physiques
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official flat fees (free registration or nominal EUR 30–120 for administrative certificates)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Articles 71-1 to 71-10 governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), as inserted by the Law of 23 July 2016
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), through the eJustice / MyGuichet electronic portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société / Pacte Social) filed for inscription in the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for an SCSp; partner contributions are contractually fixed in the partnership agreement. No escrow account or capital deposit certification requirement applies to SCSp formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription of partnership interests by each initial Limited Partner, in the amounts set forth in the Limited Partnership Agreement, be and is hereby approved; that the General Partner be authorized to execute the agreement and all ancillary instruments; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office be and is hereby established at the address recited in the agreement in Luxembourg; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Manager (Gérant) with full authority to operate the partnership's bank accounts, engage auditors, tax advisors and corporate agents; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Manager be authorized to effect all filings with the RCS, the VAT administration, and any competent authorities required to commence the partnership's business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Corporate Name and Verification of Name Availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS, via eJustice online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the proposed SCSp name and obtain a Certificate of Non-Conflict of Name. The name must include 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the acronym 'SCSp'. Electronic submission requires authentication via Luxembourg eID or Luxembourg Business Registers credentials.
required_dossiers: Copy of valid ID or passport of the applicant
Power of attorney if filed by a professional intermediary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for conflict or misleading character, submit an alternative name; the applicant may contest the refusal before the Chamber of Commerce within 15 days or file a new reservation with a revised name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (optional for SCSp unless real estate is contributed) or private deed executed by the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement setting out the SCSp's name, registered office address, object, duration, identity of the General Partner (associé commandité) and Limited Partners (associés commanditaires), and management powers of the Gérant. If any contribution consists of real estate rights, notarization is mandatory; otherwise a private deed is permitted. The registered office must be physically located in Luxembourg; a corporate domiciliation service may be engaged.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement signed by the General Partner and each Limited Partner
Consent of the owner of the registered office premises or domiciliation agreement
Identity documents and proof of address of the partners
Declaration of acceptance by the appointed Manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner notification or consent is defective, cure the defect by obtaining a retroactive ratification deed or a rectifying addendum re-executed before the same authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Substance Arrangement, and Contribution Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or banking platform licensed by the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the SCSp's name by presenting the executed partnership agreement, proof of the name reservation, and ultimate beneficial owner declarations. Although no minimum capital is required, each Limited Partner must make the contributions stipulated in the agreement (cash, in-kind, or industry/labor). The bank conducts KYC/AML due diligence, and the General Partner must provide a management declaration confirming no non-compliant business activity.
required_dossiers: Business plan or economic substance statement
Valid passport copies of partners and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC documentation, promptly provide an AML organizational chart and source-of-funds evidence; if the bank refuses the account, apply to an alternative Luxembourg or EU-licensed bank or engage a payment institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Incorporation Dossier with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS, through the eJustice / MyGuichet electronic portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation dossier electronically through eJustice: register the entity, upload the scanned partnership agreement, appoint the signatory powers, and pay the inscription fee. The RCS verifies compliance with the Law of 10 August 1915 and issues a certificate of registration allocating an RCS number. Following registration, the act is published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or caveat (e.g., missing signature or missing legalization), cure within the stated deadline by re-submitting the corrected deed; if the deadline is missed, refile the dossier with a fresh date and pay a supplementary fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Registrations: Business Number, VAT, and Tax Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre National des Sociétés et Associations (RNSA) via Guichet.lu; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS inscription, obtain or synchronize the national business number (matricule). Apply to the AEDT for a Luxembourg VAT number (TVA) for any taxable transactions; although the SCSp is generally treated as transparent for direct tax, VAT registration may be required for the sale of digital services rendered in Luxembourg. Register any employer obligations with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) if employees are to be hired.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT delays VAT registration, escalate through the dedicated taxpayer portal and submit an appeal to the Director of the AEDT within 3 months from the deemed refusal; expedite via the AEDT support desk to avoid invoicing interruptions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie (Ministry of the Economy) — Direction Générale de l'Industrie; applicable only if the SCSp directly operates physical studio production facilities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — purely digital service activity; no establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) required for the SCSp's holding and content distribution functions

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no industrial installation; office-based digital content production and streaming activities do not fall within the categories requiring a full EIA or environmental registration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not directly applicable. If incidental office operations generate regulated waste, compliance with the Law of 21 March 2012 on Waste Management and the EU Urban Waste Water Directive (91/271/EEC) standards applies; no VOC or industrial discharge thresholds are triggered at this scale.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGIDS) required for any leased office premises; workplace clearance and occupational health oversight by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) and the Service de Santé au Travail Multisectoriel under Articles L.312-1 et seq. of the Luxembourg Labor Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority; registration portal: MyGuichet.lu (Guichet.lu)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must appoint a Luxembourg service agent where required, file constitutive documents and RCS extract via the Luxembourg Business Registers, submit partner/director identification and proof of foreign tax residence to MyGuichet.lu, and apply for the national income tax registration number (NNN) and VAT identification number through the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA. Non-established taxable persons must register for VAT irrespective of turnover, typically through form 645 or via a tax representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SCSp is treated as fiscally transparent for Luxembourg income tax; no general check-the-box election is needed for pass-through status. For VAT, the SCSp is itself a taxable person if it makes supplies. Luxembourg applies hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD, and certain contractual arrangements may elect for corporate-tax transparency treatment only where expressly provided by law (e.g., collective investment fund structures).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for established businesses; non-established taxable persons have no threshold and must register regardless of turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg mandates PEPPOL-compliant e-invoicing for B2G supplies; no general real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping applies to standard B2B invoices. EU ViDA proposals and Directive 2014/55/EU govern structured e-invoicing for public procurement; private-sector clearance remains optional.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment applies to goods physically leaving the EU, provided the supplier retains transport and export evidence and the export occurs within statutory deadlines. For cross-border services and digital products (vertical micro-drama streaming, advertising, IP licensing), the place of supply determines Luxembourg VAT: B2B supplies to non-established recipients outside the EU are outside Luxembourg VAT; B2C electronically supplied services to non-EU recipients are also outside EU VAT, requiring proof of customer location, IP address evidence, and payment details.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Proof of Physical Departure from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or Bank Statement evidencing receipt of consideration
Contract or Licence Agreement identifying the non-EU buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsupported export zero-rating is treated as domestic taxable supply, giving rise to VAT due, statutory interest, fines up to EUR 10,000 per invoice, and penalties of up to 100-200% of evaded tax in cases of intentional misstatement. Input VAT clawbacks are assessed for the full correction period, and the Luxembourg tax authorities may conduct criminal fraud proceedings where export documentation is forged or manipulated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) within the Eurosystem/European System of Central Banks, supervised by the European Central Bank; banking prudential and AML supervision by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). No separate foreign exchange administration exists; exchange control competence is effectively vested in the BCL for statistics, the Ministry of Finance for policy, and CSSF for transactional integrity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full Eurozone member. The euro is freely convertible on both current and capital accounts under Articles 63-66 TFEU and the EU free movement of capital rules. There are no exchange controls, no licensing for ordinary inward/outward remittances, and no prior regulatory approval for profit distribution or capital repatriation. For a fiscally transparent SCSp, profit allocations and capital withdrawals to non-resident partners are unrestricted and are generally not subjected to Luxembourg withholding tax at partnership level. Practical hurdles are confined to strict AML/CTF due diligence, source-of-funds substantiation, and compliance with the Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (RBE). The legal form's zero-minimum capital feature may trigger enhanced scrutiny but does not impair legal convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender rules or mandatory conversion ratios exist under Luxembourg or Eurosystem law. Recipients of export revenue in foreign currencies are not required to repatriate within a fixed timeframe or sell the currency to the BCL or an authorized bank. Foreign-currency accounts may be freely maintained and managed. Receipts must, however, be accurately booked and reported for tax, statistical, and AML purposes, including through BCL balance-of-payments reporting provided by the relevant bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs), such as those authorized by the CSSF or an EEA home regulator under PSD2, may legally open e-money accounts for a Luxembourg SCSp. They offer fast onboarding, API-based transaction processing, and low-cost international transfers, but they are not credit institutions and cannot provide credit, substantial treasury services, or complex FX hedging. Legal constraints include (i) mandatory safeguarding of client funds, (ii) EMI compliance obligations under Luxembourg AML law, including full beneficial ownership identification, (iii) potential friction when the SCSp's general partner is a non-resident legal entity, and (iv) periodic transaction thresholds that limit suitability for high-value capital injections. An SCSp can use EMIs as supplementary rails for micro-drama payout distribution to creators or for small-value disbursements, but the primary clearing and settlement must remain with a tier-1 bank to ensure robust FX execution and multi-currency liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg does not statutorily mandate physical presence for KYC interviews. Under CSSF guidance, banks may onboard clients via video-call identification, qualified electronic signatures, and a notarized copy of the passport of the natural-person general partner or statutory manager. In practice, leading domestic banks accept remote onboarding for a low-risk SCSp, provided the client provides an authenticated corporate extract from the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), an RBE filing, and a signed partnership agreement. A limited number of banks (e.g., Intesa Sanpaolo Luxembourg) may require an in-person interview when the ultimate beneficial owner is a non-EEA resident or when the partnership's capital is contributed in multiple currencies. For this vertical micro-drama production and distribution structure, remote onboarding will generally be permitted for tier-1 institutions with enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership structure with non-EU limited partners and an SCSp that lacks independent legal personality under Luxembourg law.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed partnership agreement; RCS excerpt (fichier des immeubles persistent); RBE beneficial owner declaration; passport/CV for each natural person holding >25% partnership interest; country-by-country source-of-wealth documentation; organisational chart showing control and commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero minimum statutory capital and no regulatory licence for digital drama production, exposing the account to interpretation as a shell or asset-holding vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial plan for the production and global distribution of vertical micro-dramas; audited or reviewed financial projections; physical registered-office lease agreement in Luxembourg; subscription agreements with content creators; distribution contracts with Apple, Google, and streaming platform operators; substance-organisational manual describing outsourcing and local governance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket digital receipts from Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, and Stripe, which may appear as collect-and-forward payment activity rather than genuine business revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform agreements with Apple, Google, and Stripe; deposit and payout reconciliation statements; monthly revenue reports by title and territory; transfer-pricing documentation where affiliate IP licensing occurs; evidence of proper VAT and corporate tax filings for the Luxembourg SCSp and its tax adviser.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Simultaneous use of a single bank account for capital contributions and trade disbursements, creating commingling of escrow and operating funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital contribution resolutions and call notices signed by the general partner; separate internal ledger for partner contributions; explicit undertakings in the partnership agreement to maintain segregated accounts; treasury and accounting policies approved by the general partner; sworn declaration by the bank account signatories on intended usage.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections from EEA partners must be executed via SEPA Credit Transfer with the reference remarks 'Capital Contribution – SCSp Name – Purpose Code EQUI/200' where permitted, or via SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA contributors. The wire narrative must state 'Capital contribution to Luxembourg SCSp – not trade settlement' to avoid misclassification as goods/services revenue. The receiving bank will require a copy of the partner's KYC file, the executed capital call notice, and the signed partnership agreement before pass-through to the operational account. For statistical compliance, the bank will report the flow to BCL using the applicable balance-of-payments item (direct investment equity capital). The counterparty bank must be an authorized financial institution; funds from private individuals require an additional source-of-funds letter explicitly confirming the transaction is equity and not a loan. The SCSp should ensure all inbound transfers arrive in EUR where possible; foreign-currency contributions may be converted upon receipt or held in a multi-currency account, subject to the acceptable FX instruments set out below.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for production costs, creator royalties, advertising purchases, and local operational expenses will primarily use SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments within the EEA and SWIFT MT103 for cross-border non-EEA recipients. For high-frequency/low-value payouts to small content creators, the SCSp may use a PSD2-licensed EMI or a payment facilitator integrated with the video distribution app; however, all payments above a treasury threshold must anchor on the tier-1 bank's MT103 corporate trial or SEPA Direct Debits to ensure full auditability. Commercial letters of credit are generally not applicable because the business sells digital services and intellectual property licences rather than physical goods; should a co-production agreement require a documentary collection, a revolving import/export LC can be opened with the main operating bank, using the contractual cash flow projections as the basis for the facility. Prudent treasury policy requires that all outbound payments carry a standardized narrative describing the nature of the disbursement (e.g., 'Licensing fee's, 'Production service fee', 'Creator payout'), and copies of the underlying contract are retained in the bank's KYC file to avoid AML red flags.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot Contracts for same-day or T+2 settlement between EUR and USD, GBP, and other convertible currencies.
Deliverable FX Forwards (outright forwards) with a maximum maturity of 24 months, supported by documented currency exposure from app-store revenues and production expenditure.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) entered into with OECD-based credit institutions for currencies without fully deliverable local markets, strictly as hedges for projected net receipts or royalty payments.
FX Swap Contracts (short-term rollovers of matched principal and interest legs) for temporary liquidity rebalancing between the SCSp's operating and escrow accounts.
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for matching long-term multi-currency financial liabilities, subject to a documented economic hedging analysis and board approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (RBE annual declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), managed by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year between 1 January and 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 1,250 per missing declaration; criminal penalties for intentional non-compliance: fine from EUR 500 to EUR 25,000 and/or imprisonment for managers (up to 1 year)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) — required if SCSp is qualified as a large undertaking; voluntary for small partnerships
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via eCDF / Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 months after the end of the financial year (i.e., by 31 October for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine from EUR 500 to EUR 10,000 for managers; possible forced disclosure order by court; late filing exposed to civil liability and loss of legal capacity for representation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for SCSp if exceeding two of three thresholds: total balance sheet > EUR 4.4M, net turnover > EUR 8.8M, average employees > 50. Also mandatory if 10% of partners request, or if required by the articles or by court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Comptes annuels under Law of 19 December 2002) — IFRS permitted for qualifying entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SCSp must file an annual confirmation via RBE between 1 January and 31 March, declaring that the recorded beneficial owner information remains accurate. Any shareholding transfer or ownership change must be filed with RBE within 1 month of the change. The transaction update is separate from the annual confirmation window.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% corporate income tax (IRC); plus 7% solidarity surcharge on IRC and municipal business tax (e.g., 6.75% in Luxembourg City), resulting in an aggregate statutory CIT/municipal rate of approximately 24.94% before net wealth tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent and itself is not in principle subject to CIT. Partners may benefit from the participation exemption (95% dividend exemption and 100% capital gains exemption under conditions), the 80% Luxembourg IP Box deduction on qualifying IP income, and certain EU directives (Parent-Subsidiary/Interest-Royalties) for outbound payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 160 (Corporate Income Tax Return, including IRC/municipal business tax/net wealth tax declarations) or partnership equivalent; filed electronically through MyTax / MyGuichet.lu by the managing partner or tax attorney.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly estimated advance instalments are payable in months 3, 6, 9 and 12 of the tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 31 December of the calendar year following the tax year-end (12-month period from fiscal year-end); extensions may be granted on request. A fiscal year ending on 31.12.2024 is due by 31.12.2025.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered company/partnership name, legal form (SCSp), RCS Luxembourg registration number, registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a pure SCSp, insert the partnership identity; for foreign partner declarations, include the non-resident partner name and address in the annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit/loss for the fiscal year, adjusted for Luxembourg tax law (including income not subject to tax, non-deductible expenses, participation exemption, IP deduction).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the SCSp carries on a Luxembourg PE, the share of profit attributable to non-resident partners must be computed under the OECD PE profit-attribution rules and reported in this field with an accompanying PE statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying intellectual property income (IP Box): includes exempt portion (80%) and resulting net taxable IP income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may claim the IP Box deduction through the partnership allocation if the SCSp owns qualifying IP and is engaged in production/distribution activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carry-forward claimed under Article 110 LIR; state amount used in the current year and remaining balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A transparent partnership does not itself carry losses; the partner must reflect its allocable share of used and unused losses in its own Luxembourg tax position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions with affiliated enterprises requiring TP documentation; amount of inter-company royalties, management fees, interest, and capital gains; TP adjustment proposed/reverse.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must document arm's length terms with reference to the SCSp's transfer-pricing files; the Luxembourg authorities can make a TP adjustment against the partner's Luxembourg taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and dividend WHT relief claimed under tax treaties or the Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a valid TRC (certificate of residence) and confirm beneficial ownership to invoke treaty reduced rates; otherwise Luxembourg withholding rules apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 10% of the assessed tax plus late-payment interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; failure to file after formal notice can lead to forced assessment and increased penalty. Tax fraud carries fines up to EUR 250,000 and 5 years imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (Luxembourg domestic WHT on dividends from resident corporations). For SCSp, distributions are generally treated as profit allocations of a transparent partnership rather than as dividends, so no 15% dividend WHT is enforced at SCSp level. Where the SCSp is deemed commercially transparent under the applicable DTA, distributions retain their character as business profits taxable only in the partner's state if no Luxembourg PE is present.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident partner must (1) file its Luxembourg tax return or withholding-tax reclaim using Form 160/annex, (2) obtain and submit an official certificate of fiscal residence (TRC) from the partner's tax residency jurisdiction, (3) evidence beneficial ownership and absence of an artificial arrangement, and (4) specify the applicable treaty article (usually Business Profits or Dividends) and reduced rate. The Luxembourg tax administration generally grants relief through the assessment procedure or by refund of WHT withheld, without a formal pre-clearance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on outward royalties or interest payments to non-residents, provided the payee is the beneficial owner and the transaction is at arm's length. EU Interest-Royalty Directive (0% if qualifying EU parent) and tax treaties normally confirm a 0% rate; certain treaties may provide for 10-15% residual rates, but Luxembourg generally does not apply statutory withholding tax on interest/royalties absent domestic law.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1 million aggregate cross-border related-party transactions per fiscal year triggers mandatory Local File; a Master File / CbCR obligation arises for groups with consolidated turnover of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply UAE-style ESR, but it enforces substance requirements through domestic GAAR (Article 6 LIR), Article 56bis LIR on transfer pricing, ATAD anti-avoidance rules, and treaty abuse provisions. For a SCSp to benefit from tax transparency and treaty access, it must maintain real management, staff, premises, and decision-making in Luxembourg; absence of substance may result in recharacterising the vehicle as tax opaque, denying treaty benefits, imposing CIT and administrative penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Failure to File (Fraude fiscale / Absence de déclaration)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully or negligently failing to file the annual Form 160/partnership return, concealing profits, destroying accounting records, or making false declarations regarding subscription revenue (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, Stripe) of the vertical micro-drama streaming app.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud: fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil tax reassessment plus late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; late-filing surcharge up to 10%; publication of judgment in serious cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing partners/directors who knowingly approved the concealment are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, and may suffer confiscation of assets, travel bans, restitution orders, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Vehicle / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp solely to route streaming royalties and app payments while all management, manpower, contracts, and bank accounts are located outside Luxembourg; no real business purpose or local substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Invocation of Article 6 LIR (Abuse of Law) and OECD BEPS Act. The vehicle may be disregarded for Luxembourg tax purposes, profits re-allocated to shareholders/beneficial owners, treaty benefits denied, and administrative abuse penalties plus interest applied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A serious lack of substance may result in lifting the corporate veil; the general partner may be held personally liable to the tax authority for the full tax creditor; travel restrictions and custodial sentence possible if fraud is shown.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting inter-company commission, IP royalty, or app distribution fees materially different from arm's length, or failing to prepare/update the Local File. For example, charging excessive management fees to a Luxembourg SCSp from a foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg tax authorities may adjust taxable profit, disallow deductions, apply interest and penalties up to 10% of the adjustment plus 0.6% monthly late-payment interest; in gross negligence cases, criminal prosecution for tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed inaccurate TP documentation or failed to monitor inter-company pricing may be liable for the additional assessment; in aggravated cases they may be subject to a director ban and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and file ultimate beneficial owners (UBO) of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register's beneficial-ownership file, or carrying out non-IAP payment rails/withholding improperly; no suspicious transaction report filed for irregular partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines between EUR 1,000 and EUR 20,000 for failure to comply with UBO registration; in serious or recurring cases, criminal penalties up to 5 years imprisonment and exclusion from public contracts; ancillary sanctions include blocking accounts and suspension of distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing partner/directors are personally responsible for UBO declarations; intentional failure creates personal exposure to sanctions, travel bans and inability to act as director; also may be barred from accessing EU payment rails.
